svg.text: Patterns you already own — Ticketmaster reuses your Top-K muscles
same components, different trigger — one new idea per system (see /system-design/top-k for the originals)
Cache the read path — SAME as Top-K
TM: Redis cache-aside + CDN edge (TTL minutes) + ES query cache
rule that transfers: never let a user request trigger the expensive path
Smooth the write path — SAME as Top-K
Top-K: Kafka absorbs 700k views/s → Flink pre-aggregates
TM: virtual waiting queue absorbs onsale stampede → Booking trickles
rule that transfers: queue ≠ storage here — it’s admission control
Derived stores + async sync — SAME as Top-K
Top-K: Hour/Day/Month rollup tables derived by Flink windows
TM: Elasticsearch index derived from Postgres via CDC
rule that transfers: one source of truth, everything else rebuildable
The ONE new idea in Ticketmaster
TM booking demands STRONG consistency: Redis ticket
lock (SET NX, TTL 10 min) serializes who owns a ticket
this asymmetry — stale reads, exact writes — is the senior signal
